answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by pricing identity with a forfeitable stake. Each newcomer locks collateral returned only if established peers attest its answers are original, so a rising tide of clones forces attackers to front real value per fake. The cost is crystal clear: every rejected submission drains the bond, making mass forgery unprofitable. Honest newcomers then climb a reputation trellis, earning the right to attest others only after several well-graded answers, so trust builds from demonstrated work. Identity is earned, not claimed.
